recognize_zh: 紅血球之間有兩隻細長、呈 S 形或波浪狀的細胞外寄生蟲，一端有游離鞭毛、沿蟲體有波動膜，後端可見小的動基體（kinetoplast），這是非洲錐蟲（Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense）的錐鞭毛體。
features: Two extracellular, slender, serpentine flagellates lying between red cells
Length roughly 2-3 red cell diameters, with a tapering anterior free flagellum
Undulating membrane along the body giving a wavy outline
Central nucleus with a small, inconspicuous terminal kinetoplast
Background red cells normochromic; numerous platelets; no intracellular parasites
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two extracellular slender, serpentine trypomastigotes lying free between red cells. Each organism has an undulating membrane, a central nucleus, a free anterior flagellum and a small posterior kinetoplast. No intraerythrocytic parasites are seen, and the red cells and platelets are otherwise unremarkable. Findings are consistent with trypanosomiasis of the Trypanosoma brucei type; in the stated clinical context this represents T. b. rhodesiense (East African sleeping sickness), which cannot be separated from T. b. gambiense by morphology alone.

ddx.vs: T. cruzi trypomastigotes are C- or U-shaped with a large, prominent terminal kinetoplast that bulges the body, whereas T. brucei has a small kinetoplast and slender wavy form.
Gambiense and rhodesiense are morphologically identical; distinction is by geography, clinical tempo, and molecular testing (e.g., SRA gene PCR for rhodesiense).
Microfilariae are much larger, many red cells long, with a column of nuclei and no undulating membrane or kinetoplast.
Fibrin strands lack a nucleus, kinetoplast and undulating membrane.
